title: Campaign Atlas · Europe 1805 · first collection
era: French Empire and Third Coalition, September 1805
art_direction: Campaign Atlas: a war map and its armies drawn as hand-coloured engraving. Sepia ink line, gouache washes, engraver's hatching for shadow. Maps are continuous painted country; the hex grid places pieces but is never drawn into them. Interface in brass, oxblood, gunmetal and worn parchment on a lamplit desk. Tone: iron and blood, not ornament. Full statement in design/ART-DECISIONS.md.
light_direction: Upper left (north-west). Buildings, portraits and interface are lit from there with shadows cast to the lower right. Units and flags use top light only so that mirror-x facing does not reverse their lighting.

entities.label: Empire français · September 1805
entities.faction_visual: Imperial blue, white and scarlet; cocked hats and bearskins; plastered towns under clay tile with slate church spires.

relation_styles.self: Solid border in the entity colour with a pale inner glow; territory wash at full strength.
relation_styles.ally: Double ruled border in the ally's colour; territory wash at half strength.
relation_styles.neutral: Dotted sepia border; no territory wash, the land shows through.
relation_styles.opponent: Solid border in oxblood with inward hatching; territory wash at full strength in the opponent's colour.
relation_styles.unknown: Broken grey border; land dimmed under a fog wash.

global_visual.territory_style: Translucent watercolour wash over the painted map, strongest along the frontier and fading inland, so terrain stays readable. Borders and washes are separate overlays keyed to dated content records; nothing political is painted into terrain.
